Maturity Wall Framework: —
Calibration — fixture battery vs reference
Every row is one scored run of the ground-truth fixture suite (12 UCs, 9 seeded gaps, 5 controls), all scored by the same scorer. Reference rows are the ceiling — a frontier model (or human adjudication) on the identical blind pack. Nightly rows track the production model over time. The gap between them is the number a new prompt, method, or model has to close: a change is an improvement only if its row moves toward the reference without giving back precision.

AI Models Architectural review models and the UC authoring assistant
Model endpoints
Registered LLM endpoints — use flags control which DAV features each model is available in
Add model endpoint
Evaluation model
Project default for new analyses — applies to all users. Can be overridden per analysis in the New Analysis modal.
Stored server-side. Only registered model endpoints can be set as the project default.
UC Authoring model
Project default for LLM-assisted use case authoring — the Assist panel, the UC Wizard, and Bulk import all use it. Can be overridden per use.
Stored server-side. Only registered model endpoints can be set as the project default.
Architecture Review model
Project default for architectural review (Review & Plan tab) — applies to all users. Can be overridden per call from the analysis drawer's Review & Plan tab.
Stored server-side. Only registered model endpoints with use_arch_review = true are eligible.
Enhancement model
Project default for enhancement-plan generation (Review & Plan tab). Falls back to the Arch Review model when unset. Can be overridden per call.
Stored server-side. Leave unset to share the Arch Review default.
Assessment Ingestion model
Model used to parse assessment input into UDLM findings (Assessments → ingest via model). Falls back to UC Authoring → Arch Review → Evaluation when unset. Can be overridden per ingest.
Stored server-side. Leave unset to share the UC Authoring / Arch Review default.

What each role grants. Toggle cells to change a role's privileges; built-in roles can be retuned but not deleted.

Role bindings
Who is bound to what, and where — across the project and customer axes. Account bindings come from the account list above; group → role mappings are managed below.
Loading…
Bundles
Reusable, versioned packages of config/capability items (#107). Assemble once, publish a version (snapshots the items, secrets excluded), then attach to a project or use-category — it resolves there via the scope system. Editing a bundle creates a new version; attachments pin the published one.
Loading…
Agents & access tokens
Agent identities are login-less accounts (no password / SSO) that authenticate only via a Personal Access Token and carry their own roles — bound in Users & roles, exactly like a person. Create one here, grant it scoped roles, then mint a token for it. The secret is shown once.
Create agent identity
A dedicated, login-less account — separate from people. Grant it scoped roles in the Users & roles panel above, then mint a token for it below.
Mint a token
✓ Token created — copy it now
This is the only time the secret is shown. If you lose it, revoke and generate a new one.
Active tokens
All issued tokens (the secret is never shown). Revoke to disable a token immediately.
Loading…
Tenants
The hard isolation owner — 1 tenant → N projects; nothing crosses a tenant (project + customer are tenant-scoped). Phase 1 = the logical tenant + RBAC tier.
Loading…
Groups
Users → groups → roles. A group is scoped (platform / tenant / project / customer); add members and bind it to the admin/edit/view role for its scope. Members inherit the group's roles.

⚠ Approval gate
This PR would be generated from results that include UCs not in the approved state at run time. Approved UCs are the source of record for the corpus; using non-approved UCs as the basis for architecture changes weakens the audit trail.
The reason and the list of non-approved UCs will be recorded in the PR body for the corpus reviewer to see.
